missions.title: On Your Bike
missions.where: Your Flat → The Arches (Hackney Central)
missions.hook: Mo bangs on the door: rent is due Friday, and Pat "wants a word". Pat wants two bikes by tonight. Nothing fancy. Kez will show you where.

objectives.text: Get round to The Arches on Morning Lane
Nick two bikes (Graft against the lock)
Sell two bikes to Auntie Pat

missions.next: Pat has a buyer for something better: Mission 2.
missions.decision: Finish the job, buy a clean substitute off the market, hand back the one that got recognised, or give Pat an honest half-order. Whoever loses a bike today becomes somebody tomorrow — put them in the cast.
missions.consequences: A finished order opens CH2 and the storehouse stands (HC7). A disputed bike turns into a recovery Pat expects you to sort. Even short-changed, Spanner keeps the workshop open to you.
missions.campaign:
The score. Same as it ever was: Mo wants the rent, Pat wants two bikes she can sell, and the crew's got nothing but a cracked Blower and a bad attitude. Keep the opening exactly as it is — the fencing money and Pat's £40 bonus are the pay — and use it to show them the bigger yard: the Chainring Storehouse.

How it goes down.

  • FL4 and AR4: Mo at the door, Pat on the phone. Rent Friday, two bikes tonight.
  • LF1.1 London Fields Lido: a charity cycle do has left a rack of tasty bikes by the entrance. Easy pickings — until LF1.2, where someone in a club jersey clocks their own bike in your hands. Front to talk your way out, Moves to leg it.
  • HC7.2 Chainring Storehouse: Spanner gives the haul the once-over while a bloke at the roller door swears blind the second bike's his. Graft to make it unrecognisable before he gets his phone out.

Route. HC / DA / LF / DA / HC
missions.campaignTwist: Daz Riley tails the second bike all the way to the storehouse yard and leans on the shutter. Pat wants her order closed before her buyer collects at six — whoever the bike really belongs to.
missions.gm:
Start everyone in Your Flat. Walk out through Chicken Palace onto Mare Street; The Arches are round the corner on Morning Lane (the door on the Hackney map, or ride straight up to the yard).

Pat gives the order on the phone (Ask Pat for an order) or in person. Street Life puts chained bikes on every map; Kez's tip-offs are a map or two away. This is the mission to teach the lock roll, Heat (the first time someone watches), and selling at The Arches — Pat whispers an offer with a Sell button when they pull up.

GM Screen: Street → Kez's tip-off bike spawns a target near them; Checks → Spot the Old Bill before they cut the lock.
missions.twist: One of the bikes belongs to a Lea Boy. He saw. Next session he wants it back — or Stretch does.

missions.title: The Whippet
missions.where: Broadway Market (Haggerston & London Fields)
missions.hook: Pat has a buyer for a Carbon Whippet road bike — £1,800 new. The Lycra lot chain them up outside the coffee places on Broadway Market and along the canal.

objectives.text: Get to Broadway Market
Check the rack for a bait bike (Savvy, Hard)
Bring Pat a Carbon Whippet

missions.next: The Lea Boys hear Pat is paying well. Mission 3.
missions.decision: Nick or buy the right bike, flog it to a different buyer, swap buyers mid-deal, or deliver an agreed substitute. A secret switch pays now and comes back to bite later.
missions.consequences: Pat rewards the delivery once. The Spurstowe and the Barn Tavern become buyers you can ring; a robbery with witnesses gives DS Vale a tidy little lead — hello LD1.
missions.campaign:
The score. Pat's got a buyer for a Carbon Whippet. It starts at the Broadway Market coffee rack, same as ever, then the money gets complicated: a private viewing, a collector waving cash, and a fixer who sold the bike before you'd even nicked it.

How it goes down.

  • EX-BROADWAY: three Whippets on the rack — one's the real deal, one's a bait bike with a tracker in the seat post, one's already been sold twice. Savvy to tell them apart.
  • LF4.2 The Spurstowe Arms: the buyer wants a look before he pays. He's brought a mate who knows bikes. Front.
  • AR3 Chop Bay: Spanner puts it on the stand and tests it. If it's the bait, you'll know when the tracker pings.
  • HB4.2 The Highbury Barn Tavern: a collector slides an envelope across the snug table — more than the first buyer, cash, right now. Then the first buyer walks in.

Route. BG / HR / LF / DA / HC / CL / SN / HB
missions.campaignTwist: Evie Slate's already promised this exact bike to someone else. After the viewing, one buyer moves the meet and the other wants it done tonight, cash in hand, no questions.
missions.gm:
The lock is Hard. Bolt cutters make it Medium; the angle grinder makes it Easy — but it shrieks, and Broadway Market on a Saturday is full of phones (witnessed: +1 Heat).

If the owner comes back mid-job: Blag Your Way In ("I'm with the council, mate") or Leg It down the towpath. The Regent's Canal towpath runs west to Haggerston: bikes only, no police cars.
missions.twist: DS Vale has put a tracker in a bait bike on the same rack. Spot it (Savvy, Hard) or nick the bait — and a unit turns up at The Arches next session.

missions.title: Lights and Sirens
missions.where: Morning Lane → Wick Road → Hackney Wick
missions.hook: The Lea Boys have driven off with Pat's van of stripped frames from outside The Arches. Pat wants it back before it crosses the Lea.

objectives.text: Get some wheels — fast
Catch the van before Hackney Wick
Get the van back to The Arches
Deal with Stretch: pay him off, fight him, or grass him to DS Vale

missions.next: The Lea Boys come back mob-handed: Mission 4.
missions.decision: Run it down, nick it back mid-swap, buy it out, or square it with Stretch. And decide whether every frame actually goes home to Pat.
missions.consequences: A clean recovery earns Pat's Renown and opens the night shed's receiving hall (HM7). The crate's clearance papers point to HB8 Orchard Lease Office — first thread of the Quiet Ledger. Backing Stretch changes who sits across from you in LB2.
missions.campaign:
The score. The Lea Boys have driven off with Pat's van of stripped frames. Morning Lane to Waterden to Bow Breakers, like before — but one crate's already been booked onward to a depot on Orient Way, and the paperwork on it smells of new money.

How it goes down.

  • AR5 Loading Yard: what's missing, who loaded it, which way it went.
  • WW3.2 The Adam and Eve: a driver nursing a pint saw the van go. A round buys the route.
  • EX-MORNING to EX-WATERDEN: the chase, or the handover on the industrial estate. Wheels, and plenty of it.
  • EX-BREAKERS Bow Breakers Yard: the original finish line — but a crate's gone on to HM7.2 Orient Night Shed, booked under a company nobody's heard of.

Route. HC / WW / HC / WS / VW / OF / VW / WW / HM
missions.campaignTwist: Daz shifts the van just as a second buyer rolls up at Waterden. Lose it and the new holder rings with a price and a time at the night shed — come alone, bring cash.
missions.gm:
Steal something fast, or "borrow" the police area car parked on Mare Street (+3 Heat if a copper sees). Chase the van east along Morning Lane → Wick Road: each round the driver rolls Wheels against the van's driver (Opposed on the GM Screen). Track a gap from 2: a win closes it, a loss opens it; 0 = boxed in, 5 = gone.

The clever route: from the stolen area car, run ANPR on every van you pass. GM: put a marker on the van's token and the scanner flags it.

Ending on the Hertford Union bridge: Stretch and two Lea Boys. Use the Combat Console if it kicks off; the GM Screen's NPC tab can place more lads.
missions.twist: Grass Stretch to DS Vale and Pat will hear about it. She does not like grasses, even useful ones.

missions.title: Lea Boys
missions.where: The Arches, Morning Lane
missions.hook: Three in the morning. Mopeds outside The Arches, a brick through Pat's window, and somebody pouring petrol under the shutter.

objectives.text: Hold The Arches
Find out who sent them (Get Someone Talking)
Send the Lea Boys a message back

missions.next: Pat wants to move up to cars: Mission 5. And someone has been talking to the police: Mission 8.
missions.gm:
A fight in the yard. Place four Lea Boys (GM Screen → NPCs → Spawn, twice) and start a fight in the Combat Console. One has a Petrol Bomb: throw the hazard at whoever is nearest the shutter. Police turn up after three rounds if anyone fires a gun.

The one left standing talks: it was Stretch, but someone told Stretch where Pat keeps the ledger. Somebody close to Pat is talking.
missions.twist: The petrol under the shutter was not the Lea Boys' idea. Somebody paid for it.

missions.title: Chop Chop
missions.where: Bow Breakers Yard, Roman Road (Old Ford & Bow)
missions.hook: Pat introduces you to Big Den at Bow Breakers Yard. He wants a hot hatch, an estate or a hybrid — anything that sells for parts. Today.

objectives.text: Nick a car worth having (Fiester ST, Volvagen, Pious, Brixton Bruiser…)
Lose any Heat on the way
Deliver it to Bow Breakers Yard

missions.next: Hot Wheels (Mission 7) when the car jobs get serious.
missions.gm:
Cars are a step up: locks are Medium to Hard, and a relay box or key programmer (Uncle sells them from Rep 3) makes them two bands easier. A car on the street has a plate: drive past a patrol and the ANPR pings it (Clocked).

Bow Breakers is on the Old Ford & Bow map: pull up in the yard and Big Den makes an offer with a Sell button.
missions.twist: The car belongs to one of Uncle's regulars. Uncle will want to talk about it (Mission 6).

missions.title: Uncle's Errand
missions.where: Uncle's Cafe (Bethnal Green) → Roman Road Market
missions.hook: Uncle runs a café in Bethnal Green with two menus. A stallholder on Roman Road owes him £500. Uncle would like it collected, politely if possible.

objectives.text: Get to Uncle's Cafe
Take the sealed £500 envelope from Roman Road Market
Get back without being dipped or nicked
Deliver the £500 envelope to Uncle's Cafe

missions.next: Uncle's big idea: Mission 9, Westfield.
missions.gm:
The stallholder (GM Screen → NPCs → Shopkeeper) has a story: his daughter is sick, the stall was robbed, the money is "next week". Get Someone Talking, Scare Them Off or Haggle — or pay it yourself and keep the favour.

On the way back: GM Screen → Street → Pickpocket. Losing Uncle's money is a bad start with Uncle.
missions.twist: Uncle's "other menu" opens to you after this — and from Rep 3, the room out the back.

props.name: Uncle's £500 cash envelope
props.description: Uncle's sealed envelope of £500. Lift it at Roman Road Market; deliver it to the cafe area without losing it.

Find 1 × Uncle's £500 cash envelope at map LDN-OLD-FORD, area roman-rd-market. Once on the scene, look for named mission-property tokens. You must stand close enough to physically collect each item. Do not just tick a checkbox.

Deliver every Uncle's £500 cash envelope to map LDN-OLD-FORD, area roman-block-5. Hand it over from the carrier's inventory or Mission Board. A real delivery updates its objective; visiting the location alone does not count.

missions.title: Hot Wheels
missions.where: Haggerston → Kwik Spray → Bow Breakers
missions.hook: A Range Ruler SUV is waiting in a car park off Kingsland Road. It has a tracker, the owner has friends in the police, and Kwik Spray closes in an hour.

objectives.text: Pick up the Range Ruler
Lose the unmarked car on your tail
Respray it at Kwik Spray Bodyshop
Deliver it to Bow Breakers Yard

missions.next: Vale makes her move: Mission 8.
missions.gm:
The moment they drive off, set Heat to 2 (GM Screen → Police & Heat). An unmarked car follows (place a Patrol car). Lose the Police or Lose a Tail; the respray clears Heat if no unit sees them go in.

Kwik Spray is on the Haggerston & London Fields map. The respray costs £400 for a car: Pat will pay it back, eventually.
missions.twist: The tracker is not the owner's. It is DS Vale's.

missions.title: Vale
missions.where: Stoke Newington custody suite
missions.hook: DS Vale picks one of you up on a "routine matter" and buys you a coffee in an interview room. She knows about The Arches. She wants the Lea Boys — or Pat.

objectives.text: Get through the interview (Don't Grass)
Decide: give her the Lea Boys, give her nothing, or play her
Cover your tracks before Pat hears

missions.next: The raid: Mission 11.
missions.gm:
Run the interview with the GM Screen: Police → DS Vale Drops By, then Checks → Don't Grass (Hard). Each failure lets something slip; two failures and Vale has enough to raid The Arches (Mission 11 happens sooner and harder).

Giving her the Lea Boys: Mission 12 gets easier (half of Stretch's crew is arrested) but if Pat finds out (Savvy against the player's Front), the crew turns cold.
missions.twist: Vale has a grass inside The Chainring already. She lets the name slip on purpose.

missions.title: Westfield
missions.where: Westfield Stratford
missions.hook: A sports shop in Westfield takes delivery of a limited trainer drop on Thursday. Uncle has buyers for every pair. Smash, grab, mopeds, gone.

objectives.text: Case the shop (Case the Joint)
Get to Westfield Stratford
Collect the stolen Westfield goods
Get out of Stratford with three stars or less
Drop off the goods at the flat

missions.next: The Lea Boys want a reckoning on the Marshes: Mission 10.
missions.gm:
Casing it first earns one fact per success: the security guard's break, the shutter speed, the camera that doesn't work. Each fact makes the grab one band easier.

The grab is a teamwork check; the moment the glass goes, Heat 2 (3 if a guard is hurt). Westfield is next to the Olympic Park: wide roads, few hiding places, and the helicopter comes at three stars.
missions.twist: Stretch's lads are doing the same shop the same night.

missions.title: The Marshes
missions.where: Hackney Marshes
missions.hook: Stretch sends a text: a race across Hackney Marshes at dusk. Winner takes the patch west of the Lea. Loser gives up their bike.

objectives.text: Get to Hackney Marshes
Win the race (three Wheels rolls against Stretch)
Keep your bike

missions.next: Win and Stretch loses face; lose and Pat loses a patch. Either way: Mission 12.
missions.gm:
Three legs: the football pitches, the canal bridge, the Lea towpath. Each is an Opposed Wheels roll against Stretch (GM Screen → Checks → Opposed). Off-road bikes (Trailblazer, Dirt Devil) get +1 on the pitches.

A Proper Mess on the towpath: Come Off the Bike hazard — and the canal is right there (In the Canal).
missions.twist: Stretch cheats: a Lea Boy with a bike chain waits at the bridge.

missions.title: Raid
missions.where: The Arches, Morning Lane
missions.hook: Five in the morning. Kez rings, breathless: three vans on Morning Lane, a dog unit, and DS Vale with a warrant. Pat is still inside with the ledger.

objectives.text: Get to The Arches
Get Pat out the back
Save the ledger (teamwork: Search the Place)
Lose all the Heat
Physically collect 1 × Pat's rescue ledger at map LDP-ARCHES
Deliver 1 × Pat's rescue ledger at map LDP-FLAT

missions.next: Pat wants it finished: Mission 12.
missions.gm:
Set Heat 3 for anyone seen near the yard. Police → Police Dog and Hazards → CS Spray for the officers on the shutter. Officers get out of the vans and take their own turns in the Combat Console (Police AI). Surrendering is an option: Busted, but the ledger might be safe if someone else has it.

If Mission 8 went badly, Vale knows about the back door.
missions.twist: The ledger names the grass. It is someone the players like.

missions.title: Big Night
missions.where: The Lea Boys' lock-up, Leyton
missions.hook: Pat has found where Stretch keeps his stock: a lock-up behind the Leyton Orient ground. Two hundred bikes, a van of parts, and Stretch's cash box. Tonight it ends.

objectives.text: Get to Leyton
Get into the lock-up
Take Stretch's stock — or Stretch
Get everyone home
Face Pat's reckoning with the grass
Physically collect 1 × Stretch's stock crate at map LDN-LEYTON
Deliver 1 × Stretch's stock crate at map LDP-ARCHES

missions.next: Rep 6 and up: Uncle's good stuff; Rep 9, Pat's car jobs — and London beyond Hackney.
missions.gm:
The finale. Getting in: Pick a Lock, Break Down a Door, or a ram through the shutter. Inside: Stretch, four Lea Boys and a guard dog. Use the Combat Console; police arrive at Heat 3 after three rounds of gunfire, Trojans at four.

Getting the stock home is a convoy: the Tranzit van (6 seats), bikes on the back. Bow Breakers will take the van; Pat takes the bikes.

Then Pat, the ledger and the grass. Let the players decide. This is the end of "On Your Bike" — and the start of whatever they want The Smoke to be.
missions.twist: DS Vale has been watching the lock-up too. She lets them go — this time.

missions.title: The Frame Room
missions.where: Oddments Lockup · Hackney Marshes Centre · Clifden Crew Garage
missions.hook: Bought a lock-up's worth of frames in Highbury for buttons, love. Forty bikes, no questions. Then Kez spots club stickers on half of them and somebody's family papers in a saddlebag. 😬 Collector's lorry is coming for the lot tomorrow. I want it sorted before then. Sorted, not sold.
call: Bought a lock-up's worth of frames in Highbury for buttons, love. Forty bikes, no questions.
Then Kez spots club stickers on half of them and somebody's family papers in a saddlebag. 😬
Collector's lorry is coming for the lot tomorrow. I want it sorted before then. Sorted, not sold.

objectives.text: Get into the Oddments Lockup before the lorry does
Find out which bikes were donated — the club organiser at Hackney Marshes Centre
Get the dodgy bikes into the Clifden Crew Garage and work out whose is whose (Savvy)
Your call: flog the lot, give the club theirs back, keep the papers, or swap the profit for a repair contract
Physically collect 1 × Donated bike paperwork at Oddments Lockup (map LDV-HB7)
Deliver 1 × Donated bike paperwork at Clifden Crew Garage (map LDV-HC8)

missions.gm:
The score. Pat's done a bulk buy and it's gone a bit Pete Tong. The Oddments Lockup in Highbury is full of frames — some fair game, some nicked off a kids' cycling club, and one bag with a courier's whole life in it. A collector's paid a deposit on the lot and his lorry's coming. Get in, sort the wheat from the chaff, and get the dodgy ones somewhere nobody's looking.

How it goes down.

  • HB7.2 Oddments Lockup, sorting floor: forty frames, one torch, one hour. Savvy to read the stickers and frame numbers; the courier's papers are in a saddlebag in HB7.3.
  • WW1.4 Hackney Marshes Centre: the club organiser's on a Thursday committee night. She'll tell you which bikes were donated — if you don't look like the people who nicked them. Front.
  • The run: load the disputed bikes and get them across to the Clifden Crew Garage before the lorry. Wheels if you're spotted leaving.
  • HC8.2 Clifden Crew Garage: identify every bike (Graft). In HC8.4, a vehicle title in a biscuit tin — the garage could be yours one day.

Route. HB / CG / DA / HC / WW / HC

The twist. The collector's deposit was paid by Quayline Advisory — the same lot that's been buying up leases on Morning Lane.
missions.decision: Fence the lot and laugh all the way to the bank. Separate the club's bikes and send them home. Keep the courier's papers as leverage. Or take less money and a repair contract with the club.
missions.consequences: The Oddments Lockup becomes somewhere you can stash. Help the club and HC8's repair bay opens, with a tenancy on the cards. Keep the pricey groupset and its owner hires someone to come and get it.
missions.next: CH5 The Borrowed Winner · NM3 Everything Must Go · RT2 The Watch After Midnight
missions.twist: The collector's removal lorry pulls up outside HB7 after your second nose about. Two blokes, a tail lift and a clipboard. Pay them, stall them, or argue the toss — otherwise they load everything that isn't nailed down and that's that.

missions.title: The Borrowed Winner
missions.where: Leyton Orient stadium · Lee Valley VeloPark · Kingsland Courier Arch · The Kenton · Goldsmiths Riding Workshop
missions.hook: Remember that silver racer that walked off my patch in the spring? It's on a poster at the VeloPark. Resprayed, polished, entered to WIN, the cheeky sods. I could sell it. I could sell it back. Or I could get Kez's riding club a proper contract out of it. You choose — but get me that bike.
call: Remember that silver racer that walked off my patch in the spring?
It's on a poster at the VeloPark. Resprayed, polished, entered to WIN, the cheeky sods.
I could sell it. I could sell it back. Or I could get Kez's riding club a proper contract out of it. You choose — but get me that bike.

objectives.text: Blag an invite at the Leyton Orient stadium do
Find the bike at the Lee Valley VeloPark meet
Follow the bike's courier and the next handover (Kingsland Courier Arch, The Kenton)
Stop the rival rider before the prize-giving (Wheels or Moves)
Your call: deliver the score, sell it back, expose the sponsor, or buy into Kez's riding workshop
Physically collect 1 × The contested prize bicycle at Lee Valley VeloPark (map LDV-ON1)
Deliver 1 × The contested prize bicycle at Goldsmiths Riding Workshop (map LDV-HR8)

missions.gm:
The score. A bike nicked off Pat's patch has been given a respray and entered in a sponsored showcase at the Lee Valley VeloPark. The sponsor reckons it's theirs, the rider reckons it's his, and Pat reckons it's hers. Get in, get it, get out — ideally before they put it on a podium in front of the cameras.

How it goes down.

  • LY1.3 Leyton Orient stadium, hospitality: the showcase's launch do. Blag an invite and a lanyard (Front).
  • ON1.4 Lee Valley VeloPark, club room: the bike's being prepped for the meet. Graft to lift it from the stand, or wait for the race.
  • LF7.3 Kingsland Courier Arch: the courier who delivered it knows who paid. WW5.3 The Kenton: that's where the next handover is.
  • The set piece: a rival rider takes the bike out on the track towards the prize-giving. Chase him round the velodrome (Moves), nick it in the pits, or meet his price.
  • HR8.2 Goldsmiths Riding Workshop: Kez shows you what a legit future looks like — if you fund it.

Route. LY / ON / ST / VW / WS / LF / DA / HC / WW / HC / DA / LF / HR

The twist. The 'rival rider' is the original owner. He nicked it back from the thief first.
missions.decision: Hand Pat her score. Ransom it back to the sponsor for a fee. Expose the sponsor's paperwork. Or put the money into Kez's riding workshop and walk away with a future instead of a payout.
missions.consequences: The VeloPark and the stadium both open up for event work; the Courier Arch gives you dispatch contacts. Fund HR8 and you own an asset with running costs. Sell privately and the original owner is still out there, still angry.
missions.next: CH6 The Shop That Was Already Sold · GE1 The Wrong Provenance · BB2 The Wrong Winner
missions.twist: The rival rider wheels the bike towards the prize-giving with a photographer in tow. Once the sponsor presents it on camera, it's theirs in the eyes of everyone who matters.

missions.title: The Shop That Was Already Sold
missions.where: Orchard Lease Office · Essex Dry Goods · Clapton Union Rooms · Stoke Newington Town Hall
missions.hook: Bloke called Lark came in the shop today. Nice suit. Smelt of money. Offered me a tidy sum to walk away from the arches. Said half the street's already empty. It isn't. I want to know who Lark works for before I sign anything, sweetheart. Find out.

Compare offers with the workers at Essex Dry Goods and the Clapton Union Rooms
Front Lark at the property meeting in Stoke Newington Town Hall — or cut a deal
Your call: save Pat's shop and nobody else, get the street together, sell the evidence, or take Meridian's job
Physically collect 1 × Meridian acquisition schedule at Orchard Lease Office (map LDV-HB8)
Deliver 1 × Meridian acquisition schedule at Stoke Newington Town Hall (map LDV-HB5)

missions.gm:
The score. Meridian Renewal's fixer, Evan Lark, is buying Pat out — and quietly telling everyone else on the street that it's already a ghost town. It's a con. Six occupied premises have been written up as empty so they can be bought for peanuts. Pat wants the paperwork, the names, and the real price of her shop.

How it goes down.

  • HB8.4 Orchard Lease Office, deed archive: break in after hours, or blag the morning clerk. The acquisition schedule is dated weeks before any of the 'trouble' on the street. Savvy to read the dates.
  • DB8.4 Essex Dry Goods: the workers got the same offer as Pat — word for word. They're scared, not stupid.
  • CL8.3 Clapton Union Rooms: the repair office has a copy of the 'vacant' survey. Someone was living there when it was signed.
  • HB5.3 Stoke Newington Town Hall: a property meeting in the committee room. Lark's there, smiling. Front him out in public, or corner him in the car park.

Route. HB / CG / DB / CG / DA / HC / CL / SN / HB

The twist. The 'surveyor' who signed the vacant report is Esther Cole — and she didn't sign it. Somebody forged her.
missions.decision: Look after Pat and only Pat. Get the whole street to bid together. Sell the dated schedule to whoever pays most. Or shake Lark's hand and take a job with Meridian.
missions.consequences: Whatever you settle sets Pat's Renown. The six-property stitch-up becomes a real lead (E1). A private deal keeps the shop open but the neighbours find out what you signed sooner or later — and they don't forget.
missions.next: CH7 Who Runs the Arches · BM6 Who Can Promise a Home · MR5 Vacant on Paper
missions.page: CH6 · The Shop That Was Already Sold
missions.twist: Lark ups his offer to Pat the minute the tenants start comparing copies — a cheque on the counter, today only. The meeting closes one offer, but the owners and the records are still out there afterwards.

missions.gm:
The score. Turf war or treaty — it's decided in one room. Stretch wants to carve up East London's bike and van trade, and Pat would rather her crew held the pen. Get the votes, deal with Daz, and walk out with a compact people actually stick to.

How it goes down.

  • AR1 Pat's Cycle Repairs: Pat's terms, over a brew. Write them down.
  • CL7.2 Lea Bridge Social Rooms, members' room: the Lea Boys are split down the middle — Stretch's lot and Moth's lot. Find out who's wobbling.
  • OF7.3 Roman Exchange and HX7.2 Tern Wharf Dispatch: the fences and the drivers. Whoever they back, wins.
  • HC5.4 MOTH Club back room: the sit-down. Front for the talking, Savvy to spot whose debts are real, Muscle and Bottle if it kicks off.

Route. HC / CL / HC / WS / BG / OF / BG / HR / HX / DB / CG / DA / HC

The twist. The tool chest has a false bottom: Rusk's payment ledger for the 'trouble' on Morning Lane (E5).
missions.decision: Guarantee a limited peace. Back Moth. Side with Stretch. Grab the whole lot for yourselves. Or let them all split and pick up the pieces. Whatever you pick, name who pays each real debt — out loud.
missions.consequences: The compact opens the back rooms at the Social Rooms, Roman Exchange and Tern Wharf for proper talks. Threats, broken promises and public wins all turn into names — friends and enemies — who'll be back.
missions.next: CH8 Keys to the Arches · LB7 Who Speaks for the Lea Boys · TU8 The City Still Has to Move
missions.twist: Daz barges in mid-meeting with a 'recovered' tool chest and a car full of youngers ready to take it back by force. Deal with the box while the room decides whether to stay at the table or walk.

missions.gm:
The score. Endgame for the Chainring. Pat offers the crew a real stake on the same night Meridian tries to close every deal in the district. Pick a base, find the money, be in the room when the pens come out, and stop another crew walking off with something Pat pledged years ago.

How it goes down.

  • HC7.5 and HC8.4: walk round both yards with Pat. Which one's home? What does it cost a week, who's still owed, who opens up on Monday?
  • CG7.2 Glasshouse Saleroom: a buyer — or a backer — at the auction floor. Clement Wren's people are about.
  • ST7.4 Meridian Sales Pavilion, signing room: the papers. Celia's there. So's Lark.
  • Meanwhile: another crew is on its way to collect the thing Pat pledged. Wheels to beat them to it.

Route. HC / DA / CG / DA / HC / WS / VW / ST

The twist. The pledged asset is the arches' own lease. Pat put it up against a loan from Vic Randle years ago to keep Sal out of trouble — and Vic sold the debt to Quayline last month.
missions.decision: Keep it a fence. Turn it into a repair co-op. Take over the whole patch. Take Meridian's buyout. Or move the lot somewhere they'll never find it. Pat gets her say in whichever you choose.
missions.consequences: Write it down: your actual share, the keys, the kit, the debt. HC7 or HC8 becomes your headquarters for good; the other stays someone else's unless you agree otherwise.
missions.next: BM8 The Neighbourhood Gets a Vote · MR8 The City on the Brochure · AD8 The Whole City Listening
missions.twist: Rusk's collector and a tenants' delegation both turn up expecting a promise you can't give both of them. Each turn of the final night, sort one recovery or one deal — no more.

missions.where: Queensbridge Sound Store · Cafe OTO · Backspin Studio · Round Chapel
missions.hook: Big up the crew. Patch here. Got a listening night booked at the Round Chapel Friday and NO SPEAKERS. Some joker changed the hire account. Another promoter's loading MY cases into a van as we speak. Pull up, yeah?

objectives.text: Physically collect BOTH Dead Air flight cases from Queensbridge Sound Store
Find out who made the replacement booking — the performer at Cafe OTO knows

missions.gm:
The score. Patch's sound system has been hijacked by paperwork. Someone changed the name on the hire account at the Queensbridge Sound Store, and a rival promoter's already got the cases on a tail lift. No rig, no night, no station. Get it back — or get something — before the Round Chapel doors open.

How it goes down.

  • HR7.2 Queensbridge Sound Store, speaker hall: the stacks with Dead Air's gaffer tape still on them. Savvy to spot the doctored hire slip.
  • DA2.3 Cafe OTO, mix desk: a visiting performer let slip who booked the 'replacement' rig. Front.
  • DA7.3 Backspin Studio live room: Patch's HQ. Plan the snatch, or plan a smaller show.
  • HC2.2 Round Chapel event hall: the night itself — or the showdown with the rival promoter in front of three hundred people.

Route. HR / LF / DA / HC

The twist. The rival promoter is working for Owen Pike — the Velvet Circuit wants Dead Air's audience, not its speakers.
missions.decision: Nick the speakers back. Hire replacements and eat the cost. Move the whole night. Or back the rival promoter for a bigger fee and let Patch find out later.
missions.consequences: Do right by Patch and Backspin Studio's working room is yours, plus the next station job. The Sound Store becomes a hire contact; stiff a supplier and they become a creditor who rings every Friday.
missions.next: AD2 The Missing Hour · VC1 The Sound Went Missing · NM2 One Box Two Buyers
missions.twist: After your second enquiry the van starts loading. If it pulls off, it's a Wheels job through Haggerston traffic. And the Round Chapel doors open at eight whether you've got the full rig or a borrowed PA and a prayer.

props.name: Dead Air speaker flight case
props.description: One of Patch's two full-size flight cases, with DEAD AIR tape on the handles. Each holds a speaker stack, cables and a stand. You need transport to move them. Their hire account was forged: get both cases out of Queensbridge Sound Store and unload at the Round Chapel event hall.

playGuide: Patch has lost access to his hired rig. Reach Queensbridge Sound Store (HR7) and enter the speaker hall, HR7.2. Look for two separate flight cases bearing DEAD AIR tape. Both cases must be collected: they are not just a journal checkbox.

Bring a van or other suitable motor to collect the heavy boxes. Right-click each flight-case token and choose Collect. Each becomes a real gear item on the collecting character; its owner and location are tracked.

Check the replacement-booking trail at Cafe OTO (DA2). There is a performer who can tell you the other promoter's name. If a GM is not running the scene, your Blower and mission briefing tell you what you learned.
Head to Backspin Studio (DA7), the crew's live room. Agree the running order and confirm Patch's setup before the Round Chapel event.

Take BOTH speaker cases to Round Chapel (HC2). At the event hall, use Deliver for each case on the Mission Board. Delivering both clears the final job requirement. You may drop a case on the ground at any time, then collect it again.

missions.gm:
The score. Nia 'Switch' Bell, Dead Air's best voice, has gone quiet. A seller turns up with a reel of her 'latest message' — but it opens with a station ident that hasn't been used in over a decade. Someone's selling a ghost, and Patch wants to know whose.

How it goes down.

  • HR3.1 Signature Brew Haggerston taproom: a station do. The seller's at the bar in a flat cap, very keen, very vague. Front.
  • SN2.3 Abney Books side counter: the old sleeve that ident came off, in a box of records nobody's bought since the nineties.
  • DA1.3 Rio Cinema projection box: the seller's 'preview' of the reel. Listen hard — Savvy.
  • LF8.2 Englefield Listening Flat: Leon puts it all on his old deck and goes very quiet.

Route. HR / LF / DA / SN / DA / LF

The twist. The seller's a dupe. He was paid in cash by a producer who calls himself 'Bram' and never takes his sunglasses off.
missions.decision: Put an appeal out on air. Buy the reel quietly. Trade an exclusive to whoever pays. Or go on air and accuse someone — if the evidence can take the weight.
missions.consequences: That old ident opens three recording leads (E3) and Leon's listening room. Go public with a dodgy claim and you'll be issuing a correction — or making an enemy. Lose the reel and the sleeve and the seller are still out there.
missions.next: AD3 Two Stages One Van · RT1 The Empty Slot · RT4 The Night That Repeated
missions.twist: A rival buyer will have the reel before the next show goes out. The seller also swears he saw Nia 'last week' — but can't say where or when.

missions.gm:
The score. Double-booked. Two benefits, one sound system, one van, the same three acts promised to both. A sponsor's waving money to merge them under his banner. It's raining, the clock's ticking, and someone's going to end up with an empty stage.

How it goes down.

  • CG4.3 Union Chapel mix desk and HR2.2 Hoxton Hall auditorium: two organisers, two running orders, two very cross people.
  • WS4.3 The Lauriston function room: the promoters' meeting. The disputed fee is in an envelope in someone's jacket. Front to win it, Graft to lift it.
  • ON7.2 North Echo Rehearsal Rooms: a rehearsal, a replacement act, or a recording you can play if all else fails.
  • The van: Wheels to get the rig to the right stage in the rain.

Route. CG / DA / LF / HR / BG / WS / HC / WW / ON
missions.decision: Merge them into one big night. Honour one promise and break the other. Sell the exclusive. Take the sponsor's money. Or run a smaller show that's all yours.
missions.consequences: Whatever shows go ahead open backstage and rehearsal contacts at all four places. A cancelled act will work for you later, on different terms. The station's independence front moves, one way or the other.
missions.next: AD4 Pay to Play · VC3 Cash Before Curtain · BM2 Benefit Night Rain Check
missions.twist: Rain cuts both venues' capacity and the van's pulling off at six sharp. Every scene you play locks another act or another speaker to one of the two nights.

missions.gm:
The score. A protection racket on a pirate station, run in Stretch's name — except Stretch might not have a clue. Dee thinks the collector's borrowed a real volunteer's identity to make it stick. Find the impersonator before Dead Air pays for a war it didn't start.

How it goes down.

  • DA7.4 Backspin Studio edit desk: Dee's call logs and the volunteer rota.
  • HX2.2 The Eagle snug: an 'organiser' who keeps buying rounds with fifty-pound notes. Follow him.
  • CL7.3 Lea Bridge Social Rooms counting office: Moth can tell you whether this is a Lea Boys job — for a price. Savvy.
  • SN5.2 The Shacklewell Arms: the next listening night. The collector's due back. Bottle when he walks in.

Route. DA / CG / DB / HX / DB / CG / DA / HC / CL / SN

missions.decision: Pay up for a quiet life. Expose the impersonator. Rob the collection back. Partner with the Lea Boys properly. Or take a station slot as your fee.
missions.consequences: Settle it and the station trusts you. The Social Rooms and the Shacklewell open for meetings; rivals react to what they actually saw — and the fake caller still has a backer to find (E5).

missions.gm:
The score. Someone hijacked Dead Air's frequency with a threatening broadcast in Nia's voice, dragging her into the Halo panic. It's a fake stitched from old tape. An installation artist recognised the background sound; engineer Seth Calder has the rough mix and a buyer already counting notes. Get the original before it vanishes.

How it goes down.

  • VW4.2 Grow Hackney performance floor: the artist's sound installation — the same hum, the same room tone. Savvy.
  • VW7.3 and VW7.5 Wallis Tape Rooms: Seth's session notes in the control room, the master in the store. Graft.
  • HM8.2 Silt Listening Bunker: an old rehearsal tape, independent, that proves the order the pieces were spliced in.

Route. VW / WW / HM

The twist. Seth's buyer is Owen Pike. Owen paid for the fake in the first place.
missions.decision: Steal or buy the master. Broker its release to someone you trust. Publish the edit history. Or bury the lot for a faction's money.
missions.consequences: A proper side-by-side comparison proves the warning's a fake (E3). The Tape Rooms and the bunker open deeper archive work. Lose the master and the artist, the cleaner and the rehearsal tape are still routes in.
missions.next: AD6 Open Channel Loud Mouths · RT4 The Night That Repeated · VC5 A Set for Nobody

The score. Patch hands the crew a live show. Everyone wants the first word: tenants, dealers, promoters, and a sponsor with a smile you don't trust. One caller has a wild accusation; another has real paperwork that names who's been paying. What goes out on air can't be taken back.

missions.consequences: Deliver the show and you've got a real say in the station and event access. The audience, the sponsor and whoever got left out remember exactly what was said (E1).

missions.gm:
The score. Nia's alive and she'll talk — on her terms. A trusted go-between has set it up. Meanwhile three factions are offering her a car, cash or protection in exchange for her story. The crew's job: get to her first, keep her safe, and don't sell her out. Easier said than done.

How it goes down.

  • WW7.2 Willow Cabin front room: the first conversation. Asha Stone puts the kettle on and watches your hands.
  • BG8.3 Approach Recovery Rooms support room: independent support — someone who'll back Nia's account without wanting a piece of it.
  • SN8.2 Evering Safe Flat: the next hiding place. Somebody's paying for it, and they haven't said all their terms.
  • On the road: a faction driver with a better-funded offer. Wheels.

The twist. The 'independent' patron paying for the Evering flat is Celia Voss's charitable foundation.
missions.decision: Back her telling it her own way. Negotiate an exclusive. Trade what she knows for something you want. Expose where she is. Or settle for a short interview and a smaller story.
missions.consequences: Meeting her, or an account she signs off on, confirms she's alive (E4). The three hideouts open up through whoever you've kept sweet. Betray her and Nia becomes an opponent with friends of her own.
